title: Burst policy inheritance leak causing cross-environment rate-limit enforcement failures
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Production customer escalations across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments: requests are being rejected by the wrong quota/burst policy after recent routing changes. Symptoms include 429s for clients that should be in a higher burst tier, and silent enforcement for workloads that previously had relaxed burst windows. This appears correlated with token routing and policy inheritance logic in the proxy/router layer.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer with multi-tenant tokens configured for Dedicated pool sends a burst of requests
2) Proxy routes traffic through new sticky routing path (edge change rolled 2025-02-10)
3) Requests are evaluated against hosted default burst policy instead of customer's reserved burst profile
4) Observed 429s and quota counters incrementing on the wrong policy during spike window
impact: Multiple customers reported degraded availability and throttling during normal workload bursts. Affected deployments: Hosted API customers using shared routing, Dedicated customers with reserved pools, and Private customers behind the new control-plane routing shim. Business impact: live customer outages for high-throughput features, potential revenue and SLA violations.
root_cause_summary: A regression in the policy-binding path: when the proxy applies sticky routing keys it sometimes loses the explicit 'quota_profile_id' metadata (race between auth cache refresh and routing decision). The downstream quota enforcer falls back to the default environment policy rather than honoring the missing/late profile, causing incorrect enforcement. Edge case was introduced by a change to the router's cache invalidation to speed up failover.
mitigation_plan: Short-term: revert router cache invalidation change for sticky routes in the 2025-02-10 edge roll
Short-term: add emergency rule to prefer explicit profile lookups when token metadata is missing
Medium-term: add defensive read-behind for auth cache to ensure quota_profile_id is resolved before enforcement
Long-term: add unit/e2e tests that exercise race between auth cache refresh and routing decision across Hosted/Dedicated/Private modes
technical_approach: 1) Patch router: if quota_profile_id is nil, synchronously fetch from auth service instead of falling back to default
2) Add metrics and tracing annotations to policy binding path (emit auth_fetch_latency, binding_mismatch_count),
3) Harden cache invalidation: transition to versioned cache keys so stale entries aren’t temporarily empty
4) Update enforcer to log and expose the evaluated policy id in trace for sampled requests
5) Backfill tests: unit tests on router->auth handshake, integration tests via local harness simulating Dedicated/Hosted token routing
rollout_strategy: Canary patch to router in staging with 10% traffic for 24h
If stable, progressive promotion: 10% -> 40% -> 100% over 8 hours with automated rollback on error threshold
For Dedicated/Private customers with highest impact, coordinate maintenance window and apply patch directly if needed
Post-deploy: monitor binding_mismatch_count & customer 429 rate closely for 72h
qa_checks: Regression test: synthetic burst for token with reserved burst profile should not see 429s
Integration: simulate auth cache delay and ensure enforcer fetches correct quota_profile_id
Performance: verify no undue tail-latency increase from synchronous auth fetch under assumed p95 traffic
Observability: new metrics appear and trace includes evaluated policy id
